title: Critical Latency Fast-Recovery Playbook and On‑Call Toolkit
author: Marcus Li
content:
Overview:

Purpose: This playbook provides a single, opinionated response flow for critical latency incidents (service-level latency regression impacting customer-visible requests). It combines immediate triage steps, runbook playbooks for common latency root causes, escalation rules, status page and customer communications templates, and a lightweight postmortem checklist to ensure timely recovery and measurable improvements.

Scope: Applies to API services and inference routing layers that are part of the hosted Redwood API and Dedicated frontends. This doc does NOT replace component-specific runbooks for non-latency failures (eg. data-plane corruption) but should be used when P99/P95 latency spikes or sustained degradation are observed.

Owner and contacts:
- Primary on-call: API Platform SRE (team: eng-sre) — person who owns the paging channel
- Secondary on-call: Serving Runtime on-call (team: eng-serving-runtime)
- Incident lead: rotating Senior SRE/PM technical lead (assigned at incident start)

Key contacts (phone/Slack):
| Role | Team | Pager / Slack channel | Typical response time expectation |
|------|------|----------------------|----------------------------------:|
| Primary on-call | eng-sre | #pager-sre | 2 minutes |
| Serving Runtime on-call | eng-serving-runtime | #pager-runtime | 5 minutes |
| Customer Success escalation | customer-success | #cs-urgent | 15 minutes |

SLOs and Alert thresholds (config):
- Service SLOs referenced: API request P95 < 120ms, P99 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%

ASCII table for alert thresholds:
| Alert name | Metric | Trigger threshold | Severity | Initial pager? |
|------------|--------|-------------------:|---------|---------------:|
| api_p99_latency | request_p99_latency_ms | > 400ms for 3m | critical | yes |
| api_p95_latency | request_p95_latency_ms | > 180ms for 5m | high | yes |
| inference_queue_depth | queue_length | > 50 for 2m | high | conditional |
| host_gpu_utilization | gpu_util_percent | > 95% sustained 5m | critical | yes |

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes) — numbered procedure:
1. Acknowledge the pager and announce incident in #incident-redwood with: short summary, initial hypothesis, incident lead, and current pager responders.
2. Collect high-level telemetry: active request rate, P95/P99 latency trend, error rate, recent deploys (last 30m).
3. Check serving cluster capacity: GPU pool autoscaler events, node OOM logs, node replacement / preemptions.
4. Verify routing and fallbacks: are requests being routed to lower-cost/backup model variants? Is smart routing healthy?
5. Confirm whether a recent rollout or configuration change coincides with onset. If yes, mark ‘deploy-related’ and, if needed, trigger immediate rollback.
6. If no immediate hypothesis, open an incident timeline in the incident doc and assign an incident scribe.

Primary diagnostics (next 15–30 minutes):
- Run this sequence of queries/commands (examples):
  - kpi snapshots: curl -s "https://observability/api/metrics?expr=request_latency_p99[5m]" | jq
  - list recent deployments: curl -s "https://rdx-deploys/api/v1/recent?minutes=60"
  - check autoscaler events: gcloud logging read 'resource.type=container_cluster AND severity>=ERROR' --limit 50
  - inspect GPU host metrics: /opt/tools/gpu-health.sh --list-hosts | xargs -I {} ssh {} 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv'

Fast mitigation playbook (choose path based on root cause signal):
A) If GPU saturation detected:
  1) Stand up additional capacity from Dedicated reserve (if configured) using the reserve-burst policy: rdx-cli capacity allocate --pool gpu-dedicated-burst --count 2
  2) Throttle non-critical tenants via tenant-rate-limiter: rdx-cli rate-limit apply --label non-critical --p95 150ms
  3) Where possible, enable quantized model variant fallback to reduce per-token runtime: rdx-cli model fallback --model-id ml/llama-q8 --target-route /v1/generate

B) If recent deploy suspected or error increase coincides with rollout:
  1) Pin traffic to previous model version via routing policy: rdx-cli routing set --route /v1/generate --model-id ml/llama-1.2.3 --weight 100
  2) Rollback the last config change and monitor telemetry for 5 minutes
  3) Capture deployment diff and upload to incident doc

C) If queue depth/backpressure is the issue:
  1) Enable short-term request shedding for heavy batch requests: rdx-cli request-shed --predicate "payload.size>10000" --duration 10m
  2) Drain kube pod causing backpressure: kubectl cordon pod/<name> && kubectl delete pod/<name> --grace-period=30

Escalation matrix (who to call and when):
1. If mitigation not achieved in 15 minutes, escalate to Engineering Manager on-call and Product Lead.
2. If customer-facing SLA is breached (P99 > 500ms 15m window), page Customer Success and start customer communications below.
3. If incident is impacting multiple regions or is not recovering after 60 minutes, engage CTO on-call and legal for potential regulatory impact.

Escalation ASCII table:
| Time since alert | Action | Who to notify | Channel |
|------------------|--------|---------------|---------|
| 0–15m | Triage + mitigation | Primary on-call, runtime on-call | #incident-redwood |
| 15–30m | Escalate | Eng manager, product lead | pager/Slack |
| 30–60m | Customer comms live | Customer Success, comms lead | email + status page |
| >60m | Exec alert | CTO, legal | phone + Slack |

Customer communications and status page templates:
- Status page short (when acknowledging):
  Title: "Degraded latency for API requests — investigating"
  Body: "We are investigating increased latency for API requests. Some customers may experience slower responses. Our engineers are actively diagnosing and working on mitigation. We will post updates at least every 30 minutes. Impacted services: Redwood API (generation, chat)."

- Status page update (after mitigation):
  Title: "Service performance restored — follow-up action plan"
  Body: "We restored expected request latency at 14:22 UTC by rolling back a recent routing change and scaling up serving capacity. We will run a follow-up postmortem and publish findings within 72 hours. If you saw errors or delayed requests, please reach out to support@redwood.ai."

Customer email template (initial):
Subject: "Redwood API: Investigating increased request latency"
Body:
Hello <Customer Name>,

We detected elevated latency for API requests beginning at <HH:MM UTC>. Our engineers are investigating the root cause and are actively applying mitigations to restore normal performance. We will provide updates every 30 minutes and a full incident summary after the investigation.

If this incident affects your production SLAs, please reply or open a support ticket and include your request IDs or timestamps.

Sincerely,
Redwood Support Team

Customer email template (post-mitigation):
Subject: "Redwood API: Performance restored — incident summary pending"
Body:
Hello <Customer Name>,

Service performance returned to expected levels at <HH:MM UTC>. We identified the proximate causes and are preparing a postmortem. Expect the full report within 72 hours. If you observed customer-impacting errors, please share examples.

– Redwood Customer Success

Postmortem and follow-up expectations (lightweight template):
- Title: Incident: Critical Latency — <date>
- Severity: Sev2 (customer-affecting latency)
- Timeline: populate ISO timestamps with detection, mitigation, restore, and full resolution
- Summary: 2–3 sentence summary of what happened and impact
- Root cause: short paragraph
- Contributing factors: bullet list
- Action items: table with owner, description, due date, status
- Follow-ups: link to change that triggered the incident (if any), tests to add to regression suite, game-day exercise recommendation

Postmortem action item example table (ASCII):
| Action item | Owner | Due | Status |
|-------------|-------|-----|--------|
| Add P99 load test covering quantized fallback | runtime-team | 2026-03-10 | open |
| Improve alerting to include recent-deploy tag | eng-sre | 2026-02-28 | in_progress |

On-call rotations, handoff and fatigue controls:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary rotation, 1 week secondary rotation. Primary on-call should not be scheduled for more than 2 consecutive weeks without a recovery week.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled at shift start):
  - Current open incidents, links to incident docs
  - Known maintenance windows and running game-days
  - Any ongoing escalations with customers
  - Personal pager configuration verified (phones/SMS/Slack)
- Fatigue controls: auto-escalate to second on-call after 4 unanswered pages in 15 minutes; for frequent after-hours pages (>3 in 72 hours), examine traffic-shaping and paging sensitivity.

Game day design and suggested scenarios (quarterly):
- Scenario A: Sudden P99 spike due to GPU host preemption — verify autoscaler behavior, burst capacity, and fallback model selection.
- Scenario B: Bad rollout of routing policy increasing P95 latency — practice immediate traffic pin and rollback, and validate smoke tests detect this in CI.
- Scenario C: Regional outage with cross-region failover — exercise routing and data residency constraints.

Game day schedule (4 hours typical):
1. 15m — kickoff and success criteria
2. 60m — simulated incident and triage rounds, parallel tasks assigned
3. 30m — mitigation and recovery validation
4. 45m — after-action review and action-item capture
5. 30m — documentation update and follow-up task creation

Runbook appendix: commands and quick queries
- List active high-latency requests: kubectl -n api logs --tail 200 -l app=redwood-api | grep "latency" | tail -n 50
- Snapshot P99 by service: rdx-observe query 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))'
- Force traffic pinning (example): rdx-cli routing set --route /v1/chat --model-id ml/chat-1.1.0 --weight 100

Incident post-checklist (24–72 hours):
- Ensure postmortem draft is published to internal doc with owners assigned
- Verify action items have due dates and owners listed in the tracker
- Add regression tests for the proximate cause to the eval harness and CI
- Schedule a follow-up review in 14 days to validate completion of critical fixes
